_comment: Maps the review app's tag vocabulary onto the taxa the pipeline can emit, so human verdicts and pipeline predictions can be compared. A config file rather than code for the same reason taxon_map.json is: the review vocabulary changes when P adds a preset tag, and that must not be a code change.
_why_groups: The two vocabularies are at different resolutions on purpose. P tags what he can see ('deer'); the classifier names what SpeciesNet resolved ('blacktail'). Scoring 'blacktail' against 'deer' as a disagreement would measure the vocabulary gap, not the pipeline. Each group is the set of pipeline taxa a human tag legitimately covers -- agreement means the prediction landed inside the group.

roles._comment: Tags that are not species claims. They decide how a review row is used, not what it is scored against.

detector_class_groups._comment: People and vehicles are named by the DETECTOR, not the classifier. Stage 2 only classifies detector_class='animal' crops, so a correctly-detected truck carries detector_class='vehicle' and a NULL taxon forever. Scoring those against `taxon` alone charges the classifier for 31 vehicles it was never asked about, and reports a pipeline that got them right as one that got them wrong.

declined_to_name._comment: Classifier outputs that are an ABSENCE of a name rather than a competing name. A crop the classifier calls 'blank' when a bobcat was really there is a recall failure, not a confusion between bobcat and something else -- so it is counted against that tag's recall and reported separately, never entered into the confusion matrix as if 'blank' were a species the pipeline mistook it for.

deer.note: P does not distinguish blacktail from whitetail in the field and this is blacktail country; both count as agreement.

mountain-lion.note: Deliberately strict. unknown_felid is NOT counted as agreement here -- invariant 4 keeps a rolled-up felid reaching review, but scoring it as a correct lion call would hide exactly the classifier weakness that matters most.

jackrabbit.note: taxon_map v2 rolls leporidae up to the jackrabbit property prior, so the pipeline cannot reliably split the two either. Grouped rather than pretending to a resolution neither side has.

bird.note: 'bird' is the only preset for every non-turkey bird, so it has to cover the quail taxa too. Turkey has its own tag and is scored separately.

person.note: Read person precision with care. Of the captures where the detector found a person, 26 are tagged vehicle-only -- a car arriving has a driver, and the reviewer tags the salient subject rather than exhaustively enumerating occupants. So a vehicle-only verdict is NOT a reliable assertion that no person was present, and some of what scores as a person false positive is under-tagging rather than detector error. The complete-verdict assumption (invariant 9) holds for the wildlife question it was built for; it is weakest exactly here.

_unmatched_taxa_note: Pipeline taxa with no group above (domestic_cat, opossum, raccoon, unknown_canid, unknown_carnivore, unknown_felid, unknown_mammal, unknown_mustelid, unknown) have no corresponding preset tag. A prediction of one of those against any human species tag scores as a disagreement and shows up in the confusion matrix under its own name, which is the honest reading: the pipeline named something the reviewer did not.
